title: 60th sitting of the 20th Majlis

items.text: Opening recitation (Hamd and Salawat); the sitting begins.
Roll call of members present at the sitting.
Announcement of the day's agenda (Agenda No. އޖ/60/2024).
Approval of the minutes of two previous sittings (minutes Nos. 56/2024 and 57/2024).

From the Speaker's desk: the President's nominations for appointing two members to the Maldives Broadcasting Commission under Article 6(b) of the Broadcasting Act (Law No. 16/2010) are sent to the relevant standing committee for review.

From the Speaker's desk: the President's nominations for appointing two members to the Elections Commission under Article 4(b) of the Elections Commission Act (Law No. 8/2008) are sent to the relevant standing committee for review.
First reading of the Bill on Prevention of Gang Crimes and Other Dangerous Crimes, submitted on behalf of the government by Machchangolhi South MP Mustafa Hussain.
Unfinished business: continued debate on the Attorney General's Office Bill, submitted on behalf of the government by Maafannu South MP Abdulla Rifau.
Public Finance Committee report on its review of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs audit reports for 2010 to 2021.
Public Finance Committee report on its review of the Ministry of Higher Education audit reports for 2018 to 2021.
Public Finance Committee report on its review of the Foreign Currency Bill.
Public Finance Committee report on its review of the matter of compensation payments made by the State to various parties.

Economic Committee report on its review of the President's nominee for a seat on the Board of Directors of the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority under Article 4(b)(2) of the Tax Administration Act (Law No. 3/2010).
Voting on items from the day's business that have reached the voting stage.

summary: The sitting was scheduled to approve old minutes, send Broadcasting and Elections Commission nominees to committee, introduce the Gang Crimes Prevention Bill, continue the Attorney General's Office Bill, and take up five committee reports including the Foreign Currency Bill and a MIRA board nominee.
